title: Manchester City 2-2 Napoli: Cherki's late leveller spares hosts' blushes
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutManchester City 2-2 Napoli: Cherki's late leveller spares hosts' blushesShareNapoli twice led at Etihad Stadium against Manchester City, but Enzo Maresca's men fought back to claim a point thanks to Rayan Cherki.Rayan Cherki found a late bit of magic as Manchester City twice came from behind to earn a 2-2 draw with Napoli in the Champions League.
After a quiet first half, the game burst into life, with Rasmus Hojlund breaking the deadlock only for Napoli's advantage to be wiped out by Ayyoub Bouaddi's first City goal.

It looked like Noa Lang had secured all three points for Napoli, but Cherki popped up in the 86th minute to salvage a point, which means City sit sixth and do not drop out of the automatic qualification spots.
City threatened a fast start after dispossessing Scott McTominay to break on a pacy counter, but Vanja Milinkovic-Savic got down to push away Elliot Anderson's low drive.
Napoli had the best first-half chance two minutes before the break; Sam Beukema rose highest to thump Matteo Politano's corner on goal, but Gianluigi Donnarumma got fully behind it.

Ten minutes into the second half, City were caught playing out from the back, with Billy Gilmour easily intercepting a pass and sliding it through for Hojlund, who snuck his low shot under Donnarumma – who could have done better – and into the net.

That spurred City into life, with Anderson's tight-angled effort turned behind by Milinkovic-Savic, and Napoli's defence were distracted at the resulting corner. It was played short to Jeremy Doku, who pulled it back to Bouaddi to sweep his first-time finish past the goalkeeper 67 minutes in.

But Napoli restored their lead 76 minutes in with a lovely move. Politano knocked it onto Leonardo Spinazzola first time, taking Nico O'Reilly out of the game, and the right-back picked out the unmarked Lang, who volleyed past a helpless Donnarumma.
City chased an equaliser in the closing stages, with Josko Gvardiol hitting the foot of the right post, and Milinkovic-Savic denying Anderson again, but they found one last chance.
After patient build-up, Iliman Ndiaye pulled it back to Cherki, who danced his way towards the right byline in the box before beating the goalkeeper from a ridiculously tight angle.
Cherki saves City as Napoli's Champions League frustration goes on

While City have been floundering in the Premier League of late, after a run of four without a win, the same cannot be said about the Champions League, where they were chasing a third straight victory.
However, familiar problems came back to haunt them as they conceded first for the seventh time in their last 10 games in all competitions.

They have also conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time since December 2019, as former Manchester United striker Hojlund netted his ninth Champions League goal in his last 18 appearances.

But Bouaddi gave the home fans hope with what was also the first goal of his senior career, with this his 108th appearance. In fact, at 19 years and 53 days, he is the third-youngest scorer for City in the Champions League behind only Rico Lewis (17y 346d) and Phil Foden (18y 288d).

Napoli were largely organised in defence, facing 17 shots worth 1.41 expected goals (xG) in total, with Milinkovic-Savic making five saves, while they mustered just nine attempts worth 0.61 xG at the other end.
And while it looked like Lang's first Champions League goal of the season would secure Napoli's second European win of the campaign, City fought back.

Only Erling Haaland (14), Thierno Barry (10) and Nicolas Jackson (nine) have scored more goals in all competitions among Premier League players than Cherki's eight, and this goal could prove vital come the end of the league phase, with Napoli sitting 27th, outside the play-off places.
